ciphertext: 50 auth failures / 24 h / 3 distinct usernames / 47 distinct source IPs
assumptions: The 50 failures are a complete log of the window, not a sampled subset
Legitimate users in this environment access from 1–4 distinct IPs (home, office, mobile, VPN)
A credential-stuffing or password-spray tool rotates IPs via a proxy pool or residential botnet to evade per-IP rate limiting
No password-policy change, SSO migration, or authentication-UI update occurred in the prior 24 hours
The 3 target usernames have not been shared publicly in a way that would explain focused manual attempts

hypotheses.description: Automated distributed attack — targeted password spray or credential stuffing using a proxy pool to cycle source IPs while iterating passwords against 3 known target accounts

evidence.observation: 47 distinct source IPs across 50 attempts — IP-uniqueness ratio 0.94
evidence.explanation: P(0.94 IP uniqueness | automated botnet/proxy pool) ≈ 0.80; P(0.94 IP uniqueness | 3 forgetful users) ≈ 0.01. Three legitimate users working from home, office, and mobile yield at most 9–18 distinct IPs. Reaching 47 requires a distributed tool. This is the dominant evidence signal.

evidence.observation: 50 failures across 3 usernames ≈ 16.7 attempts per account per day
evidence.explanation: P(≥16 failures/account/day | attack) ≈ 0.55; P(≥16 failures/account/day | user error) ≈ 0.25. Empirically, confused users attempt 2–5 logins then call support or reset. Sixteen-plus attempts per account per day signals systematic password iteration, not confusion.

evidence.observation: Only 3 distinct usernames — atypical of classic broad-sweep credential stuffing
evidence.explanation: P(3-account focus | classic credential stuffing) ≈ 0.20; P(3-account focus | user error) ≈ 0.65. Classic stuffing sweeps hundreds of accounts using a full breached-credential list. Three-account focus refutes classic stuffing but is fully consistent with a targeted password spray against known high-value accounts — still an attack, just a narrower variant.

hypotheses.description: User forgetfulness — 3 legitimate users having authentication difficulty, retrying from multiple devices and locations after a forgotten password or session expiry

evidence.observation: 47 distinct IPs — structurally impossible for 3-user legitimate scenario
evidence.explanation: P(47 unique IPs | 3 users) ≈ 0.01; P(47 unique IPs | distributed tool) ≈ 0.80. LR = 0.013. This is the single observation that nearly eliminates H2 on its own, delivering −19.0 dB — just 1 dB shy of the refutation threshold by itself.

evidence.observation: 16.7 average failures per account — exceeds typical user retry budget
evidence.explanation: P(16+ retries | user error) ≈ 0.25; P(16+ retries | attack) ≈ 0.55. Legitimate users self-triage after 3–5 failures. Sustained retries imply a systematic process.

evidence.observation: Narrow 3-account focus — consistent with 3 users struggling with their own accounts
evidence.explanation: P(3-account focus | user error) ≈ 0.65; P(3-account focus | credential stuffing) ≈ 0.20. The only observation that favors H2. Partially offsets the IP-diversity devastation but cannot overcome it.

currentHypothesis.description: Automated distributed password spray or targeted credential attack cycling through ~1 IP per request

evidence.explanation: Near-unity IP-per-request ratio is the diagnostic signature of proxy-pool or residential-botnet tooling.
High per-account volume supports systematic password iteration over organic user retry.

evidence.observation: Only 3 usernames targeted (counter-signal against classic stuffing)
evidence.explanation: Narrows H1 sub-type: not classic broad-sweep stuffing, but a targeted spray against 3 specific accounts.

evidenceChains.hypothesis: H1: Automated distributed attack (credential stuffing / targeted password spray)

observations.observation: 47 of 50 attempts from distinct IPs — IP-uniqueness ratio 0.94
observations.explanation: LR = P(0.94 uniqueness | tool) / P(0.94 uniqueness | users) = 0.80 / 0.01 = 79.4
LR = P(16+ retries/account | attack) / P(16+ retries/account | user error) = 0.55 / 0.25 = 2.2

observations.observation: 3-account concentration — atypical for broad credential stuffing
observations.explanation: LR = P(3 accounts | stuffing) / P(3 accounts | user error) = 0.20 / 0.65 = 0.308

evidenceChains.hypothesis: H2: User forgetfulness (3 legitimate users struggling with authentication)

observations.observation: 47 distinct IPs far exceeds realistic IP footprint of 3 users
observations.explanation: LR = P(47 IPs | 3 users) / P(47 IPs | tool) = 0.01 / 0.80 = 0.013; nearly single-handedly refutes H2

observations.observation: 16+ failures per account exceeds typical user retry threshold
observations.explanation: LR = P(16+ retries | user error) / P(16+ retries | attack) = 0.25 / 0.55 = 0.455

observations.observation: Narrow 3-account focus consistent with 3 users' own accounts
observations.explanation: LR = P(3 accounts | user error) / P(3 accounts | stuffing) = 0.65 / 0.20 = 3.25 — the only favorable signal for H2

patterns.suggestion: Proxy pool or residential botnet cycling a fresh IP per request to defeat per-IP rate limiting — the defining behavioral signature of modern automated credential attacks

Inconsistent with classic credential stuffing (broad sweep of a breached list). Consistent with a targeted password spray against 3 known high-value or high-privilege accounts — a more deliberate and dangerous attack class

keyInsight: At +17.3 decibans (cumulative LR ≈ 54:1, posterior P(attack) ≈ 0.97), the automated-attack hypothesis is 2.7 dB short of formal confirmation — but the operational decision is clear. The IP-diversity observation alone contributes +19.0 dB and nearly single-handedly refutes user error. Critically, the narrow 3-account focus refutes *classic credential stuffing* (−5.1 dB) but does NOT favor user error; it fingerprints this as a targeted password spray or distributed brute force against 3 specific accounts. To cross the 20 dB threshold, collect ONE more independent signal: (a) verify that the 3 usernames correspond to admin/service/privileged accounts (would add ≈ +4 dB), or (b) cross-reference the username+IP metadata against a known threat-intel feed. Immediate mitigations without waiting: (1) emergency account lockout / CAPTCHA gate for the 3 usernames, (2) block or challenge all 47 source IPs, (3) force MFA re-enrollment for the targeted accounts. The cost of a false positive (inconveniencing potentially 3 real users) is far lower than the cost of a false negative under 54:1 attack odds.
